## Europe in 2000

In 2000, Europe had a total population of 728,164,209 people. A decade earlier, in 1990, the population was 724,139,404; it has grown by 0.6% since.

Half of the population was younger than 37.6 years; 17.6% were children under 15 and 14.7% were 65 or older. The pyramid is constrictive: cohorts of children are smaller than those of their parents, reflecting low fertility and an ageing population.

Frequently asked questions about Europe's population

What was the population of Europe in 2000? Europe had a population of 728,164,209 in 2000.

How old is the population of Europe?

The median age in Europe is 37.6 years — half the population is younger, half older.

What share of Europe's population is over 65 or under 15?

In Europe, 17.6% of people are under 15 and 14.7% are 65 or older.

What shape is Europe's population pyramid, and what does it mean?

Europe's pyramid is constrictive — narrower at the base than the middle, the signature of sustained low fertility and population ageing.
